It's become a huge problem because of the abuse of Agile/Scrum methodologies. The Official Scrum Guide is really short but no one reads it. Or they read it and then ignore it. In particular, they ignore the basic rules about the Development Team -

The Development Team consists of professionals who do the work of delivering a potentially releasable Increment of “Done” product at the end of each Sprint. Only members of the Development Team create the Increment.

Development Teams are structured and empowered by the organization to organize and manage their own work. The resulting synergy optimizes the Development Team’s overall efficiency and effectiveness.

The Development Team is responsible for determining how much they can/will get done in a sprint. The obvious objective being to move at a reasonable and even pace. Part of the objective is to actually avoid burnout and to avoid last-minute crunches. You should be able to work a consistent 40 hours/week and meet your goal. Unfortunately management loves to ignore all of this and instead dictate the milestones to the Development Team themselves. Then the sprints aren't really sprints anymore, they're death marches.

So, if you're looking for a job, find a place with good management. It makes a huge difference.

Corporate "perks and incentives" are just another type of honeypot designed by HR to keep employees away from their personal lives. It's best to minimize corporate contact as much as possible unless it directly benefits you in the form of wage increase, benefit increase (NOT perks like free food in the cafeteria, etc.) and so on.

It's a really big problem. Most programmers are salaried, which means no overtime if you work more than 40 hours in a week (or more than 8 hours in a day). This is an especially bad problem at tech darling companies (Google, Apple, etc) where you have to already be exceptional in order to even be considered. This leads to a bunch of overachievers trying out out-perform each other in an environment that already demands you put in 60+ or even 80+ hours a week, but they still get paid the same as if they put in 40. Game development is particularly bad - they exploit the fact that it's a field that a lot of young people are passionate about in order to pay them much less than they're worth.

Software developers are notoriously bad at estimating how long it will take them to implement something, and are even worse at standing up to managers/marketing. If they overestimate how long something will take, higher ups take that to mean they overestimate how long everything will take, and impose really stupid deadlines on them. If they underestimate how long something will take, well, now marketing is pissed at their manager/supervisor, who is now pissed at their devs because they got chewed out by marketing. It fosters a situation where you're damned if you do and damned if you don't. The only way to avoid it is to never deliver anything early OR late. So on the one hand you have devs delivering software that isn't done, and on the other you have devs fucking off for hours/days/even weeks at a time because delivering too early can cause just as many problems.

Management often makes the decision about what process to use (almost always something Agile, because they read a 1-page article and think 'Wow! Higher quality and faster delivery times? BETTER ALWAYS USE THAT WITHOUT LOOKING INTO IT FURTHER!!!!!') rather than the programmers themselves. In situations where Agile shouldn't be used, being forced to use Agile is a fuckin' nightmare.
